title: sliding-window-priority-admission-with-progressive-degradation-modes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: During multi-region failovers and traffic spikes we observe sharp latency SLO violations and tenant-level unfairness. Existing token-bucket and hard-priority-queue approaches either underutilize capacity (static isolation) or cause long tail latency for lower-priority tenants. Goal: implement a sliding-window priority admission controller that smooths bursts across short timescales, rebalances spare capacity between priority bands, and exposes progressive graceful-degradation modes (partial response, light model variant, compressed output) as coordinated fallbacks. The controller should integrate with circuit breakers and the multi-region routing layer so we can safely degrade during failovers without amplifying tail latency.
acceptance_criteria: New admission controller deployed behind feature flag in canary region
Emits metrics: admission_attempts_by_priority, admission_allowed_by_priority, shed_rate_by_priority, degrade_mode_active, degrade_mode_reason
Demonstrated p95 latency preservation for P0 tenants under 2x baseline traffic spike in synthetic tests
Compatibility with existing tenant token-bucket and per-model quotas (no silent bypass)
Runbook updated with playbook steps for switching degradation modes and rollback
tasks: Design: finalize algorithm for sliding-window token accounting and probabilistic admission (Ravi)
Implementation: admission controller binary + config knobs for window size, priority weights, and reallocation thresholds (Eng)
Integrations: hook into routing layer to advertise degraded-capable model variants and circuit breaker state (Infra)
Observability: add Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards plus alerting rules for shed_rate and degrade_mode duration (SRE)
Testing: synthetic spike harness across two regions and chaos test for region failover (QA)
Canary rollout: feature flag gating and stepwise traffic ramp with automatic rollback on SLO regression (Eng Ops)
Documentation & Runbook: author operator-facing guide and incident playbook (PM)
Postmortem plan: collect telemetry for first 72 hours after GA and run retrospective
design_notes: Windowing: use 10s sliding window with 1s resolution for admission smoothing; window size configurable per deployment
Allocation: each priority band has a soft-share and hard-minimum; soft-share can be borrowed by lower bands probabilistically when utilization < 70%
Probabilistic admission: when spare tokens insufficient, accept requests with probability p = spare / requested to avoid synchronized drops

Graceful modes: enumerate modes in order of increasing degradation cost - (1) response-compression, (2) partial-field responses, (3) light-model variant (quantized/shorter context), (4) request-trimming + hint to client
Circuit breaker integration: open CB if shed_rate for P0 exceeds configured threshold for 30s; on open, trigger prioritized fallback routes and cross-region reroute
Multi-region failover: on region-congestion signal, progressively shift non-P0 lanes to secondary region while enabling mode (3) for lower-priority tenants
Telemetry: annotate requests with admission_decision and degrade_mode for per-tenant analysis
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: probabilistic admission could create client confusion if partial responses returned frequently. Mitigation: add response headers and SDK signal flag to surface degrade_mode and suggested retry semantics.
Risk: cross-region reallocation may increase egress/cost. Mitigation: make cross-region borrowing opt-in per-tenant with configurable budgets and quota alerts.

Risk: misconfiguration causes systemic over-shedding. Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout, staged canary, and auto-rollback on SLO alerts. Add safety circuit that ensures P0 latency budget is evaluated globally before shedding P0.
observability_plan: Metrics: admission_attempts_by_priority, admission_allowed_by_priority, shed_rate_by_priority, degrade_mode_active_count, degrade_mode_duration_seconds
Traces: hook admission decisions into per-request trace as tags (admission.window_spare, admission.p, degrade_mode)
Dashboards: create 'Admission Control' dashboard with per-tenant and cluster-level views and anomaly detection for sudden shed spikes
Alerts: P0_shed_rate > 0.5% for 60s, any degrade_mode_active for > 5m for >10% of tenants in a region
rollout_plan: Phase 1: merge code behind feature flag, unit & integration tests (non-prod)
Phase 2: canary in single availability zone at 1% traffic for 4h, collect metrics
Phase 3: canary across region pair at 5% traffic for 24h with chaos failing a region to validate failover behavior
Phase 4: gradual ramp to 25% and enable automatic rollback on SLO regression alerts
Phase 5: GA behind tenant opt-in for cross-region borrowing, monitor 72h telemetry
